name: Georgian Khinkali
description: Khinkali, Georgia's famous soup dumplings, are genuinely eaten with a specific ritual, not just any way you like - real technique keeps the filling deliberately juicy so it creates its own broth inside as it cooks, sealed with a real twisted top called kudi (meaning 'tail'), which is traditionally left uneaten and counted at the end of the meal. Real etiquette picks the dumpling up by the kudi with your hand, never a fork, since piercing the dough spills the broth and misses the entire point.

ingredients_full.note: tsp, for the real, non-negotiable garnish

ingredients.note: tsp, for the real, non-negotiable garnish

steps_detailed: Mix the flour with enough water to form a smooth, elastic dough. Rest 15 minutes.
Mix the beef with the onion, garlic, cilantro, cumin, and a splash of water, kept deliberately a little wet so it releases real broth as it cooks.
Roll the dough thin and cut into rounds.
Place a spoonful of filling in the center, gather the edges into pleats, and twist firmly at the top to seal completely - this real twisted kudi is what holds the broth in.
Boil in salted water 8-10 minutes until they float and the dough turns translucent.
Crack fresh black pepper over the top immediately - real tradition treats this as essential.
Eat by hand, holding the kudi: flip upside down to pool the broth, take a small bite from the side, slurp the broth, then eat the rest, leaving the kudi itself on the plate.

name: Georgian Khachapuri
description: Khachapuri, Georgia's iconic cheese-filled bread, is genuinely made with real yeasted dough sealed completely around the cheese, real Imeretian-style technique pressing the dough flat again after sealing so the cheese distributes evenly throughout, not just in the center.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour and baking powder with warm water and the melted butter into a soft dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Mix the feta and gruyere together for the filling.
Roll the dough into a round, place the cheese in the center, gather the edges up and seal completely, then flatten gently again so the cheese distributes evenly.
Brush with the beaten egg and bake at 400F (200C) for 18-20 minutes until deeply golden.

name: Georgian Lobio
description: Lobio, a real bean stew seasoned with walnuts and coriander, is a genuine Georgian staple, real technique cooking the beans down until the sauce thickens naturally.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Beans, kidney, all types, mature seeds, canned
ingredients_full.note: standing in for real dried beans

Add the beans and a splash of water, and simmer 15-18 minutes.
Stir in the ground walnuts and cilantro, and simmer 5 minutes more until thickened.

name: Georgian Pkhali
description: Pkhali, real vegetable pâté bound with ground walnuts, is a genuine Georgian staple, real technique blending the walnuts finely enough that the mixture holds together when shaped.
steps_detailed: Boil the spinach 3-4 minutes, then drain very well and chop finely.
Blend or mix with the ground walnuts, garlic, and vinegar until it holds together.
Shape into small balls or a mound before serving.

name: Georgian Chakhokhbili
description: Chakhokhbili, chicken stewed with a real large amount of fresh herbs and tomatoes, is a genuine Georgian home-cooking staple, real technique adding the herbs generously at the end so their flavor stays bright.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and garlic, and simmer 25-28 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Stir in the cilantro generously at the end, off the heat, so its flavor stays bright.

name: Georgian Ajapsandali
description: Ajapsandali, a real vegetable stew of eggplant, pepper, and tomato, is a genuine Georgian summer staple, real technique salting the eggplant first to draw out bitterness.
steps_detailed: Salt the eggplant and let sit 15 minutes, then pat dry.
Cook the eggplant and bell pepper in a little oil, 8-10 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and garlic, and simmer 12-15 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro at the end.

Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.
